newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Committee passes S.African development bank bill.
newsitem.headline: Committee passes S.African development bank bill.

text.p: The parliamentary finance committee on Monday approved an amended bill giving a legal status to the Development Bank of Southern Africa (DBSA).

The bill, which was first presented to the committee on February 18, was sent back because it did not believe that the bank had consulted interested parties widely enough nor taken their concerns into consideration.
Concern had been expressed that the bank might compete unfairly with commercial banks, the Land Bank and development finance institutions.
The committee threatened to hold public hearings if the bank did not liaise with interested parties and allay some of their concerns.

Finance department director general Maria Ramos and DBSA chief executive Ian Goldin briefed the committee on consultations that had taken place and said that all concerned now appeared satisfied with the bill and the changes made.
"Everyone is now on board," she said.

There was some debate about whether the bill should specify that DBSA would concentrate on providing wholesale finance for infrastructural projects but it was agreed that it should be provided with a broader mandate.
In terms of the amended bill, the bank will no longer be incorporated in terms of the Companies Act but its name will be entered in the registry of the Registrar of Companies.

Formed in 1983 through a treaty between the former South African government and its so-called black homelands, DBSA was thrown into a legal limbo by the adoption of a new constitution after the country's first democratic elections in 1994.
